title: Watch: Moment a government building collapses into a river in Nepal amid floods
summary: The municipality building in Baglung was left teetering on an unstable ledge due to floods before it fell into a river.
text: Nepal government building falls into a river amid heavy flooding - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat Asia China India Watch: Moment a government building collapses into a river in Nepal amid floods Watch: Moment a government building collapses into a river in Nepal amid floods Close Massive flooding left a government building in western Nepal teetering on the edge of an unstable ledge before it fell into the Daram River. Witnesses captured the moment that the building in Baglung collapsed on Sunday, 27 September. Officials removed important documents and computers from the building before it fell, local ward chair Tej Thapa confirmed to the BBC. No one was injured. Landslides and floods have killed at least 27 people over recent days, according to Nepal's national disaster agency, only weeks after a flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border killed 1,400 people and left thousands more missing.
